newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope ordains 12 bishops in Epiphany mass.
newsitem.headline: Pope ordains 12 bishops in Epiphany mass.

text.p: Pope John Paul formally consecrated 12 new bishops from around the world on Monday, including the priest named to lead a new diocese in Indonesia's mostly Roman Catholic territory of East Timor.

Bishop Basilio Do Nascimento was named last week by the Pope to head the newly created diocese of Baucau covering the territory's eastern half. He assumes duties as apostolic administrator of the new diocese in March.
East Timor previously had only one diocese, led by Nobel laureate Bishop Carlos Belo. He remains leader of the diocese based in Dili.
Belo, an immensely popular figure in the territory, was jointly awarded the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize with self-exiled East Timorese independence advocate Jose Ramos Horta.
Belo has a long-standing record of speaking out against Indonesia's sometimes harsh rule in East Timor. He has equally called for the restless youth in the territory to stop fighting.

Indonesia invaded East Timor in December 1975 before declaring the territory its 27th province the following year, an act not recognised by the United Nations which still regards Portugal as the administering power.
The Pope traditionally consecrates new bishops during mass to celebrate the feast of the Epiphany, the day the Church commemorates the visit of the Magi to the infant Jesus.
The other new bishops consecrated by the Pope during the mass in the Vatican's St Peter's Basilica on Monday were:
Luigi Pezzuto of Italy, Vatican ambassador to Congo and Gabon.
Paul Sardi of Italy, special ambassador assigned to Vatican's office of Secretary of State.
Varkey Vithayathil of India, apostolic administrator of diocese of Ernakulam-Angamaly.
Delio Lucarelli of Italy, bishop of Rieti.
Ignace Sambar-Talkena of Togo, bishop of Kara.
Luciano Pacomio of Italy, bishop of Mondovi.
Angelo Massafra of Italy, bishop of Rreshen in Albania and apostolic administrator of the diocese of Lezhe.
Florentin Crihalmeanu of Romania, assistant bishop of Cluj-Gherla.
Jean-Claude Perisset of Switzerland, assistant secretary of the Pontifical Council for the Promotion of Christian Unity.
Piotr Libera of Poland, assistant archbishop of Katowice.
Hil Kabashi of Albania, bishop of Torri di Bizacena.
